title: Chain Rule
description: Learn how to use the chain rule to find the derivative of composite functions.
content: The chain rule is a formula to compute the derivative of a composite function. If f and g are differentiable, then the chain rule expresses the derivative of their composite f ∘ g in terms of the derivatives of f and g and the functions themselves.

title: Product Rule
description: The product rule for finding the derivative of two functions multiplied together.
content: In calculus, the product rule is a formula used to find the derivatives of products of two or more functions. It may be stated as: (fg)' = f'g + fg'.

title: Quotient Rule
description: Learn the quotient rule for differentiating ratios of functions.
content: The quotient rule is a method of finding the derivative of a function that is the ratio of two differentiable functions. It states: (f/g)' = (f'g - fg') / g^2.

title: Power Rule
description: The most fundamental rule for derivatives: d/dx(x^n) = nx^(n-1).
content: The power rule is used to differentiate functions of the form f(x) = x^n, where n is a real number. The rule states that the derivative is f'(x) = nx^(n-1).

title: L'Hôpital's Rule
description: Using derivatives to find limits of indeterminate forms.
content: L'Hôpital's rule provides a technique to evaluate limits of indeterminate forms (0/0 or ∞/∞) using derivatives.

title: Integration by Parts
description: A technique for integration based on the product rule for derivatives.
content: Integration by parts is a process that finds the integral of a product of functions in terms of the integral of the product of their derivative and antiderivative.

title: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
description: The theorem that links the concept of differentiating a function with the concept of integrating a function.
content: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus is a theorem that links the concept of differentiating a function with the concept of integrating a function. It consists of two parts: the first part deals with the derivative of an antiderivative, while the second part provides the method to evaluate definite integrals using antiderivatives.

title: Implicit Differentiation
description: How to differentiate equations where y is not explicitly isolated.
content: Implicit differentiation is a technique used in calculus to find the derivative of an algebraic function when the dependent variable depends on the independent variable in an implicit way (e.g., x^2 + y^2 = 25) rather than an explicit one (y = f(x)).

title: Partial Derivatives
description: Find derivatives of multivariable functions with respect to one variable at a time.
content: In mathematics, a partial derivative of a function of several variables is its derivative with respect to one of those variables, with the others held constant. It is used in multivariable calculus and vector calculus.

title: U-Substitution
description: The integration counterpart to the chain rule.
content: U-substitution is a method for finding integrals. Using the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, it corresponds to the chain rule for differentiation. It involves replacing a complex part of the integrand with a single variable 'u'.
